locations.rationale: Instance method call `invoice.audit` where `invoice` is `Billing::Invoice.build`, which returns `Invoice.new`. Invoice's ancestor chain is [Formatting, Invoice, Auditable, Record, ...]; neither Formatting, Invoice, nor Record defines `audit`, so the call resolves to Auditable#audit, mixed in via `include Auditable`.

Exact identifier token `audit` in the literal symbol argument of `invoice.public_send(:audit)`. The receiver is statically a `Billing::Invoice` instance and the symbol is a compile-time literal, so the dynamic dispatch provably invokes Auditable#audit through the include chain; per rule 1 it semantically resolves to the declaration.

records.rationale: The declaration is instance method `audit` in module Billing::Auditable (auditable.rb line 2, chars 8-13). Invoice mixes it in with `include Auditable`; `prepend Formatting` and superclass Record do not shadow `audit`, so both call sites in app/report.rb (the direct call on line 7 and the literal-symbol `public_send` on line 14) resolve to it. The string literal "audit" in the method body (auditable.rb line 3) and the `require_relative "auditable"` string are string content, omitted per rule 3. The `Auditable` constant references are usages of the module, not this method. Ruby method mixins produce no explicit import/export binding tokens, so no optional binding locations exist under the bindings_optional policy.
